s00.note: t=0: the rod lies flat on the board next to the grey peg plate, and the locate fit agrees with the tracker to 0.6 mm. Grasp attempt 0: k03 (t=2.36) shows the open fingers straddling the rod, which runs perpendicular to the closing axis. The close was done by the servo with no keyframe of its own, and it reported width 8.9 mm with a large downward force (F=[-15,13,-47] N). During the close the TCP drifted about 2 mm in y. After the lift, k04 (t=5.16) shows the rod still on the board, the fingers fully shut (width -0.0002) and nothing in the wrist view between them. The re-located centre had moved about 6 mm, so the close pushed or rolled the rod instead of pinching it. Attempts 1 (k07-k10, t=6.4-9.96) and 2 (k13-k16, t=11.2-14.76) went the same way: width about 9 mm at close, Fz -66 and -70 N, rod left on the board each time and nudged a little further (k16 shows it on the board, slightly turned). The 50-70 N downward force at close means the fingers were pressing into the board or onto the top of the rod while closing. The rod was squeezed away instead of held. Grasp FAIL at t=15.6, insert never ran, and the arm stayed idle until the 40 s timeout. Final sheet frames (t=18-40) show the rod lying on the board, not in the fixture.

locate.evidence: t=0 frame: rod lying on the board, untouched. Fit n=3384, rms 0.17 mm, length 49.2 mm, axis horizontal, centre z=0.013. Agrees with the tracker to 0.6 mm.

grasp.evidence: Three closes, each about 9 mm wide with Fz -47/-66/-70 N. After every 7 cm lift (k04 t=5.16, k10 t=9.96, k16 t=14.76) the rod is still on the board and the fingers are fully closed (width about 0). The rod was pushed or rolled a few mm each time. The policy's FAIL verdict is correct.

insert.evidence: Never ran because grasp FAILed. At the end the rod is lying on the board, not in the fixture.

s01.note: t=0: the rod lies flat on the board beside a grey upright post. Locate passed (n=2747, rms 0.17 mm, length 49.8 mm). Grasp: k02 (t=3.08) shows the pre-close above the rod. The close gave width 3.4 mm, which is much narrower than the 8 mm rod diameter. So the rod was held only by the fingertip edges, not squarely between the pads. k04/k05 (t=6.56/6.68) do show the rod lifted in the fingers about 8 cm above the board, sticking out sideways, and the wrist view shows it between the fingers. Insert: the reorientation move_to_joints (t=6.68 to 11.6) turned the TCP z-axis horizontal. By k06 (t=11.6) the width is -1.1 mm (fingers fully shut, hand empty) and the rod is lying horizontally to the right of the post, away from the hand. The wrist view in the sheet at t=8.0 already shows the rod tilted and separate from the fingers. So it slipped out early in the reorientation. The arm then went down over the fixture empty (k07 t=12.28), and insert FAILed at t=12.52 with 'rod not seen in hand'. That reason is correct, but the rod was lost during transport, not during alignment. The arm stayed idle until the timeout. In final.png the rod is still lying horizontal near the right edge of the board, out of the hand and not in the fixture. The tracker had lost the part after the grasp (it reports z=-0.0036 from t=6.68 on) and should be ignored.

locate.evidence: t=0: rod flat on the board, untouched. Fit rms 0.17 mm, length 49.8 mm, axis horizontal ([-0.01,-1,0]), centre z=0.013. Agrees with the tracker to 0.4 mm.

grasp.evidence: k04/k05 (t=6.56/6.68): rod in the fingers about 8 cm above the board, and the mask-fit centre went from z 0.013 to 0.082. The promised state was reached. But the width of 3.4 mm, far below the 8 mm diameter, shows the rod was held only by the fingertip edges. That weak hold is why it fell out in the next stage, so the grasp needs to put the pads squarely around the rod.

insert.evidence: The rod slipped out of the hand during the move_to_joints reorientation (t=6.68 to 11.6): the width fell to -1.1 mm and k06 shows the rod lying horizontally away from the hand. The arm reached the fixture empty, there was no insertion attempt, and in final.png the rod is lying on or at the edge of the board, not in the fixture.
